regions.region: page 1 title, abstract, author block, DOI, and ESI availability sentence
regions.finding: Verified the source title and aggregate kinetic-resolution/carboxylation claim. The article states ESI availability, but workspace SI association remains unestablished and no SI fact was imported.

Three generic prior-work routes to optically active tertiary propargylic alcohols were classified as literature examples: asymmetric alkynylation, nucleophile addition to ynones, and kinetic resolution. They are not current-paper experiments.

Three generic prior-work routes to axially chiral tetrasubstituted allenes were classified as literature examples: direct allene functionalization, 1,4-enyne functionalization, and CPA/quinone-methide conjugate addition.
The Pd((R)-DTBM-SEGphos)Cl2/acid/H2O/CO/toluene current-paper reaction is a general scheme; experiment-specific Table 1 and Schemes 2–4 records are kept separate.

unresolved: Scheme 1 prior-work structures use generic R/X groups and do not define unique experiments.
The current generic arrow does not print an experiment-specific time or scale.

regions.finding: Narrative review of prior allene strategies and the authors' earlier ligand-supported protocols; bibliography/prior work was not expanded into current-paper experiments beyond the generic Scheme 1 classifications.

regions.region: page 2 upper-right Table 1 header, entries 1–10, and footnotes
regions.finding: Ten independent optimization runs were retained with row-specific acid loading, temperature, time, product/byproduct NMR yields, recovered-alcohol yields, HPLC ee values, explicit dashes, and the 20 mol% PPh3 footnote for entries 1–2.
The prose identifies entry 7 as optimal for recovered (S)-1a and entry 8 as the shortened 12 h route to (S)-2a. These statements map to the table rows and are not duplicate runs.
The prose introduces the Scheme 2/3 experiments shown on page 3 and supplies no additional independent run beyond those displayed entries.

unresolved: Table 1 omits workups, purifications, isolated masses, and isolated yields.
Dashes are source markers and their detection meaning is not defined.

regions.region: page 3 left Scheme 2 header, 20 product drawings, values, and footnote
regions.finding: Twenty independent recovered-propargylic-alcohol scope experiments were retained with common charges/conditions, row times, recovery, ee, selectivity factor, and the 12 mol% acid overrides for 1o and 1t.

regions.region: page 3 upper-right Scheme 3 header, 25 product drawings, values, and footnote
regions.finding: Twenty-five independent allenoic-acid scope experiments were retained with common charges, row times, NMR yields, HPLC ee, printed selectivity factors, and the 4 mol% catalyst override for 2u. No s value is printed for 2x/2i/2j/2u, so none was inferred.

regions.region: page 3 lower prose and gram-scale/synthetic-application discussion
regions.finding: The prose supplies outcomes for the Scheme 4 scale-ups and transformations and is linked to the page-4 arrows. The rac-1f run has separate allenoic-acid yield and recovered-alcohol recovery.

unresolved: Scheme 2/3 omit workups, purifications, isolated masses, and several analytical details.
Scheme 3 does not print s for 2x/2i/2j/2u.
Compact scope structures are label-based candidates with structure_verified=false.

regions.finding: Two independent rac-1a scale-ups were retained: 1.03 g scale recovery of (S)-1a (42%, 92% ee) and the 50 mmol/10.12 g run using 1.5 mol% Pd to give 4.24 g (S)-2a (36% isolated, 90% ee).

Four distinct transformations of (S)-1a were retained with every caption reagent/loading and row outcome. The red-Al sequence is split into −78 °C/1 min, an untimed warming transition, and room-temperature/6 h stages; arrow 4 preserves its explicit 96% ee starting sample note.

Seven distinct operations were retained: one two-product rac-1f kinetic resolution, three (S)-2f transformations, successive resolution of (S)-1f, Weinreb-amide formation, and allenone formation. The 0 °C→r.t./3 h and −78→0 °C/1 h programs are timed transitions rather than flattened temperatures.

regions.region: page 4 right Scheme 5 SAESI-MS panels a–d
regions.finding: One standard-condition reaction mixture analyzed after 10 min gave source-assigned ions at m/z 1320, 1470, and 1534. The panels are analytical outcomes of one experiment, not isolated preparations.

unresolved: Most Scheme 4 arrows omit scale, workup, purification, isolated mass, and measurement basis.
The 50 mmol scale-up does not restate time or solvent volume.
SAESI-MS cannot distinguish MS-Int. III from III' and does not establish isolation.

regions.region: page 5 upper-left Scheme 6 and mechanism prose
regions.finding: The Pd(II) reduction, anti-SN2' oxidative addition, CO/H2O carboxylation, reductive elimination, and slow-substrate recovery form one proposed catalytic cycle. Proposed species are not treated as isolated experiments.
The m/z 1534 assignment is explicitly MS-Int. III and/or III'; it remains linked to the page-4 analytical experiment with unresolved isomer identity.
Conclusions add no new reaction. The acknowledgment that Yizhan Zhai reproduced (S)-1h, (S)-1j, and (S)-2l is provenance on existing Scheme 2/3 records; no independent run details are supplied.
Bibliography/prior literature only; references were not expanded into current-paper experiments.

unresolved: The cited ESI Table 1 was not associated or imported.
The reproduction acknowledgment does not define separable runs.
Mechanistic intermediate structures remain source assignments and machine-unverified.

regions.region: page 6 left and right columns, references 2–7
